title: Learn DSA With an AI Coach, Not Just Videos
subtitle: 7 prompts turn ChatGPT into your personal tutor
intro: Tutorials made you watch. ChatGPT made you think, says Minhaz. What if the same 7 questions could fix your mistakes at your pace?
takeaway: Prompt engineering turns AI into a personal DSA tutor, but you must verify its answers.

sections.heading: Analogy: A coach, not a video
sections.body:
Learning from a tutorial is like watching a basketball video. It plays the same for everyone.

Learning with AI is like a coach watching you. Prompt engineering means writing clear instructions so the AI teaches to your level, your mistakes, and your pace.

With the right prompt, it can explain intuition, break a problem down, and spot your bug, which is why it exists.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Personal help without paid courses
sections.body:
Tutorials teach everyone the same way and can't see your code.

Minhaz's 7 prompts fix that. They ask AI to build concept intuition, debug your code, break problems into steps, recognize patterns, and analyze time and space complexity. Time complexity means how runtime grows, space complexity means how memory grows.

It's personalized learning with AI, without paid courses. But personal help has a price, shown next.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When your coach is wrong
sections.body:
An AI tutor can hallucinate a wrong answer or a weak complexity analysis and sound confident.

If you copy without testing edge-cases, you learn the mistake, not the pattern. Pattern-based problem solving only works if you practice and verify.

Use prompts to think, then test the code yourself.
